Change 7. Well supported with some lexical exceptions; the typical outcome is l in South Halmahera and Raja Ampat languages and r in Cenderawasih Bay and Mamberamo languages (PCEMP *dua 'two' > Sawai -lu, Yerisiam rúu-hí). Exceptions: Raja Ampat d in *dəŋəR and r in *ma-diŋdiŋ; Umar and Yaur d in *dua (p. 182).
Change 8. Based on only a few reflexes, but attested across SHWNG (*zalan 'road' > Taba lolan, Moor ràrin-a). Umar, Yaur and Yerisiam apparently have *z > ∅ (four reflexes in all) (p. 182).
Change 9. Attested across SHWNG, but with substantial irregularity: the change was probably not complete in PSHWNG, though a precursor was present (p. 182). Decision shwng-k.
*k survives as k in some words across the region, particularly in South Halmahera languages and Moor (*kayu 'wood' > Gebe kay; *manuk > Gane manik). Decision shwng-k.
Change 10. Generally well attested outside Raja Ampat (*ənəm 'six' > Buli wonam); in Raja Ampat later vowel changes obscured the result (p. 182).
Change 11: PMP *a, *ə > *a in final syllables (*tanəm 'to plant' > Gebe fa-tanam).
Change 13: irregular *ə > *e in PMP *pəñu 'green turtle', attested across SHWNG; the only exception is Umar ono (pp. 182-183).
PMP *ŋ > ∅ (*laŋit 'sky' > Yerisiam ráakátè; *taŋis 'cry' > Yaur ʔàáh-rè). Loss of a nasal in all positions is unusual, but a single innovation does not firmly establish the subgroup.
PMP *R > ∅ (*Rumaq 'house' > Gane um, Sawai um; *wahiR > Sawai wɔɛ, Taba woya).

PMP *t > k > ʔ in Yaur (as in Moor), after which ʔ > ∅ except word-initially on verbs; Yaur has no phonemic word-initial glottal stop on other parts of speech (p. 185 and n. 7). PEMP *pat 'four' > r-ía-hè; *tunu > ʔún-dè.
